newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares seen up despite U.S. market break.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares seen up despite U.S. market break.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed in early trading on Friday and traders saw new funds pushing up the record-breaking low-liquidity market despite lower activity from the U.S. due to the Independence Day holiday.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index edged up to a record 482.51 at the opening after Thursday's record 481.13 close.
"We don't see any end to the trend, though gains over the past week have been phenomenal," said a Moscow trader.
Western orders driving the market were drawn to oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS, which rose to $22.76 at 0855 GMT from $22.50 at the previous close.
International long-distance operator Rostelekom RTKM.RTS, which firmed to $4.995 from $4.790, was rising on this week's announcement that a level-two ADR programme was almost ready.
National electricity company UES EESR.RTS built on recent sharp gains, rising $0.4480 from $0.4470.
Traders said they saw volumes lower as U.S. participants sat out for the day, but did not see the Western-driven first-tier market flagging.
Rinaco-Plus trader Alexander Starchenko said less liquid second tier stocks were looking up, partly boosted by rouble demand.
"The holiday will not have a very significant effect on the market," he said, saying he did not see any correction on Friday despite the hot gains of the last two days when the RTS set records.
"Judging by what's happening on the market now, there's no basis for expecting that."
